content:
I've been using the iPhone Air for a full year and just switched to the iPhone 18 Pro a week ago. While both phones have their merits, the biggest takeaway after using the iPhone 18 Pro is — absolutely zero compromises. Let me explain.

iPhone 18 Pro: The most powerful camera system, longest battery life, and top-tier performance

If you're in the market for a new iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro is almost certainly one of your top choices.

This week I'm using the wine red version, which replaced my iPhone Air. While I loved the Air, the 'zero compromises' philosophy of the iPhone 18 Pro is really hard to beat.

  • The camera on the iPhone 18 Pro is significantly better than the Air in both quality and features. The telephoto and ultrawide lenses come in very handy in specific scenarios, and even the main lens performs better on the iPhone 18 Pro.
  • Battery life is equally impressive. When I was using the iPhone Air, I found the battery adequate for daily use, but I occasionally had to top up at noon. After switching to the iPhone 18 Pro, I no longer have to worry about battery life at all.
  • Performance is also excellent. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone run incredibly smoothly, and Siri's AI responses are much faster. With the added Vapor Chamber cooling, the phone has never overheated — an issue that happened occasionally with the Air.

I'm not a professional photographer, and if you're looking for battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance's iPhone 18 Pro review covers everything. After using the iPhone 18 Pro for a week, the word 'outstanding' keeps popping into my head.

The iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) features Apple's most premium camera system to date, offers the best battery life, and outperforms every other model. I also noticed some subtle improvements: the built-in speakers sound better, and the upgraded Dynamic Island is quite eye-catching.

All of the above are quantifiable differences, but what I appreciate even more is the peace of mind that comes from knowing my iPhone has Apple's 'best of the best' hardware in all the most important areas. No more wondering: would family photos look better on another iPhone? Would this lag not happen on a different model?

Setting aside all the merits of the iPhone 18 Pro, I have to admit I'm also very intrigued by the upcoming iPhone Duo.

iPhone Duo: Like the iPhone Air, imperfect but extremely appealing

The iPhone Duo shares a lot in common with the iPhone Air. Beyond similar design language, both come with their own shortcomings.

Just like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo's camera system will fall short of the iPhone 18 Pro. Battery life may be comparable but certainly won't match the Pro Max, and sustained performance may also be somewhat lacking. The iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action Button.

However, despite these compromises, I'm still very much looking forward to trying the phone in person.

Because it brings a number of innovations that the iPhone 18 Pro doesn't have. The foldable design could be the most important hardware change in iPhone history.

This week I've been completely immersed in the iPhone 18 Pro experience. But guess what? A few days ago when I picked up the iPhone Air again...

I immediately said: 'Wow.'

After using the Air's slim form factor for a full year, I'd taken it completely for granted. But after spending a few days with the iPhone 18 Pro, I rediscovered just how forward-looking the Air's design is. I expect the iPhone Duo will deliver a similar experience — not just in design, but in actual everyday use.

I'm genuinely excited about the prospect of fitting an iPad-like experience into my pocket. Even if it means putting up with the Duo's shortcomings, that anticipation hasn't diminished at all.

The era of Apple offering a single 'ultimate' iPhone is over. If you want a phone with zero compromises, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are the perfect choice. But if you're after a more forward-looking, more unique experience, I still can't wait to try the iPhone Duo.

What are your thoughts on the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo? Feel free to share in the comments.
